title: εἰ and εἶ
note: εἰ is a proclitic and has no accent of its own; εἶ, from εἰμί, has a circumflex.

title: ἡ, ἥ, and ἤ
note: The article ἡ is a proclitic, with no accent; the relative ἥ has a rough breathing and an accent; the conjunction ἤ has a smooth breathing.

title: ὁ and ὅ
note: The article ὁ has no accent; the relative ὅ (neuter) has one.

title: οὐ and οὗ
note: οὐ, not, has a smooth breathing and no accent; οὗ, of whom or where, has a rough breathing and a circumflex.

title: ἐν and ἕν
note: The preposition ἐν is a proclitic with a smooth breathing; ἕν, one, has a rough breathing and an accent.

title: εἰς and εἷς
note: The preposition εἰς is a proclitic with a smooth breathing; εἷς, one, has a rough breathing and a circumflex.

title: ἦν and ἥν
note: ἦν, from εἰμί, has a smooth breathing and a circumflex; ἥν, the relative, a rough breathing and an acute.

title: ὤν and ὧν
note: ὤν, the participle of εἰμί, has a smooth breathing and an acute; ὧν, the relative, a rough breathing and a circumflex.

title: ἀλλά and ἄλλα
note: The conjunction is accented on the last syllable; ἄλλα, other things, on the first.

title: αὐτή and αὕτη
note: αὐτή, from αὐτός, has a smooth breathing on the diphthong; αὕτη, this, a rough breathing.

title: τίς and τις
note: The interrogative always keeps its acute; the indefinite τις is an enclitic, often written without an accent.

title: τί and τι
note: The same pair in the neuter: τί asks; τι, enclitic, is indefinite.

title: πῶς and πως
note: πῶς asks; πως, enclitic, is indefinite.

title: ποῦ and που
note: ποῦ asks; που, enclitic, is indefinite.

title: πότε and ποτέ
note: πότε asks; ποτέ, enclitic, is indefinite.

title: ἄρα and ἆρα
note: ἄρα draws a conclusion; ἆρα, with a circumflex, asks a question.

title: κρίνει and κρινεῖ
note: Liquid verbs form the future with a contraction, so present and future differ only in the accent: κρίνει, he judges; κρινεῖ, he will judge.

title: μένει and μενεῖ
note: Another liquid verb: μένει, remains; μενεῖ, will remain.
